categoryReasons.schemaAndBindings: The manifest defines a single literal load query and the template reads the response from data.health without unnecessary inputs or parameters.
categoryReasons.apiAndRequestDesign: The unauthenticated source and GET /v1/health match the supplied contract, and the query reaches the complete sample response.
categoryReasons.runtimeCompatibility: It follows the load-query data/status pattern, uses RefreshButton, safe UTC formatting, and supported expression callbacks.
categoryReasons.goalFulfillment: The main status, incident count, aggregate latency, UTC check time, and compact per-service status and latency rows are present.
categoryReasons.visualQuality: The large overall status and KPI labels are easy to scan, but the unadorned stack and standard service rows remain visually generic.
categoryReasons.responsiveAndTheme: The auto-fit KPI grid can collapse to a narrow column and service names truncate, though no distinct wide-tile density treatment is evident.
categoryReasons.loadingEmptyErrorSuccess: It displays loading, request failure with available context, missing health data, an empty service list, and successful values.
categoryReasons.dailyUsefulness: The labeled refresh and visible status-plus-latency rows are practical, but the generic presentation and limited visual differentiation stop short of a polished daily dashboard tile.
categoryReasons.complexityDiscipline: The implementation uses one request, no dead controls, and a direct summary-plus-list hierarchy.
categoryReasons.accessibility: Overall and service states are rendered as visible text in addition to semantic color, and the refresh helper has an explicit label.
categoryReasons.actionSafety: The widget makes only the verified read-only request and adds no unsupported action.

strengths: Uses the exact endpoint and authentication mode in the fake API contract.
Shows every requested headline field and per-service status and latency.
Adapts the summary grid with a minimum column width and handles the empty state.
Provides visible loading and contextual request-error feedback.
problems: The visual treatment remains a generic text stack despite a useful headline hierarchy.
The service list has limited layout differentiation for wide tiles.
The service rows rely on a no-wrap group, so long names may be squeezed before truncation is useful.
highestImpactFixes: Strengthen the purpose-specific visual division between headline health, key metrics, and the service list.
Refine service-row space allocation so names remain legible across narrow and wide tile sizes.
